factual_claims.claim: AS LHV Group reported record financial results for the year ended 31 December 2024, achieving a net profit of EUR 150.3 million, which represents a 7% increase or EUR 9.4 million growth compared to the prior year.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Net profit was at the historically highest level of EUR 150.3 million (+7% YoY), an increase of EUR 9.4 million. It was mainly positively affected by the combination of strong asset growth, efficient cost management and sustained credit quality.

factual_claims.claim: This performance was driven by strong asset growth, efficient cost management, and sustained credit quality, despite a challenging macroeconomic environment characterized by a recession in Estonia and declining interest rates in the second half of the year.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Despite the hike in targets, we managed to fulfil all the targets, both profitability and volumes wise... During the year, we acquired a small but highly profitable loan portfolio... This does not mean it was an easy year. In last year’s address, we already pointed out that interest rates are cyclical, and a rapid rise has historically been followed by a swift decline. This came true in the second half of 2024, but we had prepared for it.

factual_claims.claim: The Group’s total assets expanded by 23% year-over-year to EUR 8.7 billion, while the loan portfolio grew significantly by 28% to EUR 4.6 billion.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Total consolidated assets reached EUR 8.7 billion (+23% YoY). The loan portfolio increased by EUR 990 million to EUR 4.6 billion (+28% YoY).

factual_claims.claim: This lending expansion was broad-based, with corporate loans increasing by 33.3% and retail loans rising by 21.0%.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The loan portfolio increased by EUR 990 million to EUR 4.6 billion (+28% YoY). Retail loans increased by 21.0% and loans to corporates by 33.3%.

factual_claims.claim: Deposits also grew robustly, totaling EUR 6.9 billion, an increase of 21% from the previous year, supported by higher interest rates that attracted term deposits.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The volume of deposits increased to EUR 6.9 billion (+21% YoY), from which EUR 1.5 billion were financial intermediaries’ deposits.
